# CORRIDRA — IMPLEMENTATION CANVAS v1.0

Production-grade execution plan for Final Architecture v1.0

**Status:** Architecture implementation baseline — editable.


## 0. Architecture Freeze

**Product:** Corridra — cross-border market-access infrastructure that converts commercial missions into qualified counterparties, verified meetings, field evidence and measurable commercial outcomes.

**Three native engines:**
- Mission Infrastructure
- Diaspora Commerce Grid (DCG)
- Commercial Outcome Graph

**Commercial products generated by those engines:** supplier missions, buyer sourcing missions, trade-fair yield, market-entry missions, distributor/customer searches, institutional cohorts and corridor programmes.

**Non-negotiable architecture rules:**
1. One modular, multi-tenant, EU-primary platform; not separate products.
2. PostgreSQL is canonical transactional truth.
3. Source ≠ claim ≠ evidence ≠ verification ≠ canonical fact ≠ inference ≠ recommendation.
4. Global/public organisation truth is separated from tenant-private commercial knowledge.
5. Every material commercial state change emits an immutable domain event.
6. AI is provider-agnostic, policy-controlled and never owns permissions, money, verified facts or legal decisions.
7. Outcome Graph is generated from ordinary operations; no graph database initially.
8. Operations-first UX: humans can deliver paid missions before every external portal exists.
9. Frictionless buyer UX: no registration required merely to accept/decline an introduction.
10. Advanced infrastructure is added only when measured load or product evidence justifies it.


## 1. Stakeholder Reality Model

| Stakeholder | Field reality | Corridra response |
|---|---|---|
| Bangladesh supplier/exporter | Wants buyers quickly; may overstate readiness; hates long onboarding | 3–5 minute mission intake; progressive evidence; claims remain self-declared until verified |
| Spanish/EU firm entering BD | Wants accountable local execution, not another dashboard | Concierge-first mission; visible outcomes; platform complexity stays backstage |
| Buyer/procurement person | Scarce attention; spam-averse; unlikely to register for one meeting | Secure magic-link page: relevance, evidence, accept/decline/request info |
| EU sourcing buyer visiting BD | Wants 5–10 relevant factories, not a directory | Requirement-first sourcing mission and verified shortlist |
| DCG participant | Engagement is inconsistent unless task, reward and evidence are explicit | Mobile-first task board; precise reward; fast verification; reputation by capability |
| High-value diaspora connector | Protects relationships; may reject gig-style work | Private connector mode; introduction attribution; higher-value success economics |
| Chamber/embassy/trade body | Often spreadsheet/programme driven; wants accountability | Cohort import/export, outcome dashboard, PDF/CSV/API; no forced workflow replacement |
| Local agent/partner | Protects contacts and wants credit/revenue | Relationship ownership, selective visibility, contribution attribution |
| Internal Ops | Will fall back to WhatsApp/Excel if slower than manual work | Ops Console is the fastest route to next action |
| Admin/founder | Needs control but creates systemic risk if omnipotent | Versioned configuration, approvals, reversible changes, audit trail |

## 3. Concrete Technology Stack

| Layer | Initial choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Language | TypeScript, strict mode | One language across web, domain, workers and AI |
| Package manager | pnpm workspaces | Fast, deterministic monorepo |
| Build orchestration | Turborepo | Simple monorepo boundaries/caching; optional, not architectural dependency |
| Web | Next.js App Router, current stable pinned | Vercel-native delivery and strong server/client boundary |
| UI | React + Tailwind + accessible component primitives | Fast iteration without locking business logic into UI |
| Validation/contracts | Zod + generated OpenAPI where external APIs exist | Runtime validation + typed contracts |
| ORM/migrations | Drizzle ORM + SQL migrations | SQL visibility, typed schema, easy Postgres features/RLS |
| Primary DB | Neon PostgreSQL, EU region | Branching, serverless Postgres, Vercel integration |
| DB extensions | PostGIS, pgvector | Geo missions/nodes; embeddings without extra datastore |
| Jobs | Transactional outbox + Vercel Workflow | Durable orchestration while keeping business-event truth in Postgres |
| Queue | Postgres/outbox initially | Avoid beta/extra dependency; add dedicated queue only when required |
| Files | EU-region S3-compatible storage | Evidence/document durability and lifecycle controls |
| Auth | Better Auth or equivalent behind IdentityProvider adapter | Low-cost, app-controlled identity; preserve future OIDC/SSO migration |
| AI SDK | Vercel AI SDK inside Corridra AI Gateway | Consistent streaming/structured calls, while Corridra owns policy/routing |
| AI transport | Direct adapters initially; optional Vercel AI Gateway in production | Provider portability without business-code dependency |
| Telemetry | OpenTelemetry + Sentry/Vercel observability | Trace web→AI→workflow→DB→outcome |
| Testing | Vitest + Playwright + integration/RLS tests | Fast unit, end-to-end and authorization regression coverage |
| IaC | Terraform/OpenTofu when infrastructure surface expands | Reproducible environments without premature complexity |
| CI/CD | GitHub Actions + Vercel Git integration | PR checks + preview deployments + controlled promotion |

```text

├─ packages/

│  ├─ auth/                        # identity-provider adapter + authorization helpers

│  ├─ opportunities/               # pipeline, RFQ, proposal, contract, invoice, cash
│  ├─ communications/              # channel adapters, templates, opt-out/policy checks
│  ├─ compliance/                  # data class, purpose, retention, jurisdiction rules
│  ├─ integrations/                # email/maps/storage/payment/company-data adapters
│  ├─ ui/                          # shared accessible design system

│  └─ config/                      # typed runtime configuration
├─ docs/
│  ├─ architecture/
│  ├─ adr/
│  ├─ threat-model/
│  ├─ data-governance/
│  ├─ api/
│  └─ runbooks/
├─ scripts/
├─ .github/workflows/
├─ AGENTS.md                       # Codex rules and architecture guardrails
└─ README.md
```

**Boundary rule:** UI/routes call application services; application services call domain + repositories/adapters. No route or component performs direct database writes. One domain module never updates another module's tables directly; it uses commands/services/events.


## 5. GitHub Operating Model

**Repositories:** one private GitHub repository initially (`corridra/corridra` or founder-owned equivalent). Split only when security/team boundaries require it.

**Protected `main`:** no direct pushes. Required pull request, passing CI, migration checks, RLS tests, typecheck, lint, unit/integration tests and preview smoke test. Require at least one review once a second trusted engineer exists.

**Branches:** short-lived `feat/*`, `fix/*`, `chore/*`, `security/*`. Avoid long-running environment branches.

**Required GitHub controls:**
- Secret scanning + push protection.
- Dependabot/Renovate.
- CodeQL for supported languages.
- Signed/verified commits where practical.
- CODEOWNERS for auth, migrations, AI policy, compliance and payments.
- Branch protection; no force-push to `main`.
- Release tags and change log.

**PR template must answer:** problem, architecture impact, data migration, privacy/security impact, AI behavior impact, tests, screenshots, rollback plan.

**Migration rule:** every schema change is forward-compatible, reviewed SQL, reversible where feasible, and tested against a fresh database plus an upgraded database.


## 6. Codex / Agent Development Contract

`AGENTS.md` is authoritative for coding agents. Codex must never infer architecture from nearby code if an ADR says otherwise.

**Mandatory agent rules:**
1. Read `docs/architecture`, relevant ADRs and module README before editing.
2. Work only on one PR-sized task packet at a time.
3. Never push directly to `main` or production.
4. Never print/reveal secrets or production personal data.
5. Never bypass RLS/service authorization to make tests pass.
6. Never change canonical state machines, evidence semantics, money ledger or AI policy without an ADR.
7. Add/update tests with every behavior change.
8. Add migration + rollback/mitigation notes for schema changes.
9. Preserve structured audit/domain events for commercially material actions.
10. AI-generated code is treated exactly like human code: review, tests, static analysis, preview verification.

**Task packet format for Codex:**
- Required outcome
- Relevant modules/files
- Acceptance criteria
- Explicit non-goals
- Data model/API changes
- Security/privacy constraints
- Tests required
- Preview verification steps
- Rollback notes

**Codex completion gate:** `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm test:integration && pnpm build` plus Playwright for changed user flows.


## 7. Environments: GitHub → Vercel → Neon

```text
FEATURE BRANCH / PR
        │
        ├─ GitHub CI: lint/type/test/security/migration checks
        │
        ├─ Vercel Preview Deployment
        │       │
        │       └─ isolated Neon PREVIEW branch from SANITIZED non-production parent
        │
        └─ Playwright smoke/e2e against preview

MERGE TO MAIN
        │
        ├─ production migration gate
        ├─ Vercel Production deployment
        └─ Neon PRODUCTION database (never preview-parent source)
```

**Databases:**
- `corridra-prod`: production only, EU region, PITR/backups, restricted identities.
- `corridra-nonprod`: synthetic/sanitized seed data; parent for preview branches.
- Every PR gets an isolated branch/database through Neon/Vercel integration or automation.

**Critical rule:** never create preview environments by cloning production data. Neon branching is excellent technically, but the preview parent must be non-production/sanitized.

**Environment variables:** separate Vercel Development/Preview/Production scopes. Production credentials are unavailable to Preview.


## 8. Neon Database Model and Tenancy

**Two knowledge spaces:**

```text
GLOBAL / REUSABLE
 organisation
 public_company_fact
 country / region / market
 sector / category / product_taxonomy
 public_identifier

TENANT-PRIVATE
 organisation_relationship
 private_contact_data
 mission / mission_participant
 commercial_intent
 target / match_assessment
 outreach / meeting / follow_up
 opportunity / rfq / sample / proposal / commitment / contract / invoice / cash
 private_note / negotiation
 evidence_access
 dcg_assignment / contribution / reward
```

**Every tenant-private row carries `tenant_id`.** Use PostgreSQL Row-Level Security plus application authorization. RLS is defense-in-depth, not a replacement for service-level permission checks.

**Core identifiers:** UUID/UUIDv7-style application IDs. Store external/source IDs separately. Never expose sequential internal database IDs.

**Data types:** money as integer minor units + ISO currency; timestamps as `timestamptz`; geography via PostGIS; mutable low-frequency extensions via schema-validated JSONB.

**Deletion:** soft-delete where operationally necessary; privacy deletion/anonymization is an explicit workflow and audit event, not arbitrary row deletion.

## 10. State Machines and Commercial Truth

**Mission:** `DRAFT → QUALIFICATION → ACTIVE → TARGETING → OUTREACH → MEETINGS → FOLLOW_UP → COMMERCIAL_PIPELINE → CLOSED`, with explicit `CANCELLED` and `ON_HOLD` branches.

**Meeting:** `PROPOSED → ACCEPTED → SCHEDULED → HELD`; alternatives `DECLINED`, `CANCELLED`, `NO_SHOW`, `RESCHEDULE_REQUIRED`.

**Opportunity funnel:** `LEAD → QUALIFIED_OPPORTUNITY → PROPOSAL → COMMITMENT → CONTRACT → INVOICE → CASH_COLLECTED → RECURRING_REVENUE`, with `LOST` available from defined states and mandatory loss reason.

**Evidence:** `SUBMITTED → UNDER_REVIEW → VERIFIED | REJECTED | EXPIRED | SUPERSEDED`.

**DCG task:** `OPEN → RESERVED/ASSIGNED → IN_PROGRESS → SUBMITTED → VERIFIED | REJECTED → REWARD_APPROVED → PAID`.

Transitions are server-side commands, never UI-only status edits. Every state change emits a versioned domain event with actor, timestamp, causation and correlation ID.


## 11. Evidence, Provenance and Trust

**Truth pipeline:** `Source → Claim → Evidence → Verification → Canonical Fact → Inference/Score → Recommendation`.

A supplier-entered capacity claim remains `self_declared`; it does not become verified because AI extracted it from a PDF. A DCG visit, certificate verification or buyer history may increase evidence quality, but original claims are retained.

Every important record can answer: who said it; source; observation date; validity window; verifier; confidence; visibility; data classification; AI-use policy; retention rule.

**Files:** encrypted EU object storage; database stores key, hash, MIME, size, uploader, classification, provenance and retention. New evidence creates a new immutable object; old files are not overwritten. Malware scan and MIME verification precede availability.

**Entity resolution:** deterministic identifiers/domain/address first, AI similarity second, human review for ambiguity. All source records remain traceable after canonical merge.


## 12. DCG Operating Model

**DCG is a commercial participation network, not a social feed.** Home shows clear missions/tasks and economics rather than asking users to complete a profile for its own sake.

**Task types:** verify business, shelf/price audit, structured interview, sample delivery, trade-fair observation, local introduction, meeting assistance, distributor validation, follow-up support.

**Anti-gaming:** timestamps, evidence hashes, duplicate detection, source metadata, optional task-level coarse geolocation, counterparty confirmation, reviewer checks, cross-node corroboration, anomaly signals. Do not continuously track people.

**Contribution attribution:** one opportunity can credit signal originator, decision-maker introducer, local meeting support, platform research and commercial closer separately.

**Ledger:** append-only entries, never editable balance. Status buckets: pending, approved, available, reserved, paid, reversed. Money stored in minor units/currency.

**Payout reality:** phase 1 keeps ledger and manual/legal-review payouts. Do not automate global payouts until country, work-status, tax and payment-provider rules are validated.


## 13. AI-Native Control Plane

```text
DOMAIN MODULE
   ↓ AI task request
CORRIDRA AI GATEWAY
   ├─ tenant + permission check
   ├─ data classification / PII policy
   ├─ provider eligibility
   ├─ task + prompt version
   ├─ cost / latency / health routing
   └─ model selection
         ├─ Gemini adapter
         ├─ OpenAI adapter
         └─ Anthropic adapter
                ↓
        structured output validation
                ↓
        confidence / risk gate
          ├─ auto-accept low-risk
          └─ human review
                ↓
           AI execution lineage
```

**Provider contract:** `generate`, `generateStructured`, `embed`, `vision`, `toolCall`, `stream`, `healthCheck`, `estimateCost`.

**Business code never checks provider names.** It calls a task such as `counterparty_fit` or `document_extract`.

**Admin may route enabled/configured providers without deployment.** Raw API-key creation remains DevOps/KMS controlled initially; the Admin panel stores only credential references/status, never retrievable plaintext secrets.

**Use Vercel AI SDK for provider ergonomics, not as the policy authority.** Corridra Gateway owns classification, routing, budgets, human-review and audit. Vercel AI Gateway may be enabled later/production as transport/failover, but Corridra can also call provider adapters directly.


## 14. AI Task Registry and Safe Automation

**Initial AI tasks:** company enrichment, public-company research, entity-resolution suggestion, document extraction, commercial-intent extraction, buyer/supplier fit reasoning, target suggestion, meeting brief, translation, field-evidence extraction, follow-up suggestion, opportunity summary, duplicate/anomaly explanation.

Each task has: input schema, structured output schema, allowed data classes, allowed tools, prompt version, provider/model routes, max cost, timeout, evaluation set, quality threshold and human-review rule.

**Initially autonomous:** summarize, translate, extract, classify low-risk public/internal data, suggest matches.

**Human approval required:** external outreach, commitment/pricing, payouts, eligibility/legal determination, suspension, verified-fact changes, confidential document sharing, commercial acceptance/signature, destructive deletion.

**Free Gemini development rule:** public, synthetic, test or irreversibly redacted data only. Do not send buyer negotiations, personal contacts, confidential pricing, contracts or customer evidence through a provider/tier whose terms permit content use for product improvement.

**Model switching gate:** run candidate provider/model against versioned golden evaluation cases; compare correctness, hallucination, schema adherence, cost, latency and safety before promotion.


## 15. Communications and Outreach Compliance

Communications are first-class records: conversation, message, participant, channel, purpose, legal/policy basis, opt-out status, delivery/reply/thread.

Support institutional introduction, referral, event/network introduction, buyer opt-in, official company channels, permitted email, phone/manual outreach, platform message and DCG introductions. Do not make unlimited AI cold email a core growth assumption.

Before production in Spain/EU, counsel reviews GDPR, LSSI/ePrivacy outreach rules, controller/processor roles, legitimate-interest assessments, consent language, international transfers and retention.

No LLM or automation decides that a channel is legally permitted. Jurisdiction policy engine + human-approved rules decide; AI can classify or suggest.


## 16. Security and Privacy Baseline

**Identity:** MFA/passkeys for privileged users; session revocation; least privilege; step-up auth for sensitive operations.

**Authorization:** RBAC + ABAC. Attributes include tenant, organisation, mission, relationship owner, country, purpose and data classification. RLS covers private rows; application authorization remains mandatory.

**Application:** TLS, HSTS, CSP, CSRF protection, secure cookies, rate limits, bot/WAF controls, SSRF defenses, strict input validation, output encoding, secure upload pipeline.

**Secrets:** Vercel encrypted environment secrets initially; move to dedicated KMS/secret manager when dynamic credential administration is required. Never store retrievable provider keys in application tables.

**AI:** prompt injection treated as untrusted-content problem; no database credentials; no arbitrary SQL; scoped tools; permission checks outside model; consequential tool calls require deterministic validation/human gate.

**Privacy:** purpose limitation, minimisation, retention, DSAR/export/delete workflows, consent versioning, international-transfer controls, legal hold. EU-primary storage; Bangladesh/other-country access is role/purpose restricted and contractually governed.

**Audit:** immutable events for permissions, exports, verification, payouts, AI routing/policy changes, config changes, deletion, admin activity and security events.


## 17. Vercel Deployment and Workflow Strategy

**Vercel responsibilities:** Next.js hosting, edge/CDN/WAF surface, Preview deployments, Production promotion, environment separation, runtime logs/observability, durable Workflows.

**Workflow use cases:** mission orchestration that pauses for external response, post-meeting follow-up, evidence processing pipeline, scheduled mission reminders, AI evaluation runs, document-processing chains, institution report generation.

**Do not replace the Postgres transactional outbox.** Business transaction + domain event + outbox row commit atomically; a dispatcher starts durable workflows. This preserves replayable commercial truth even if orchestration technology changes.

**Vercel Queues:** keep outside critical architecture until Corridra needs direct high-volume pub/sub and the product maturity/operational requirements justify it. Current Vercel documentation lists Queues as public beta; Workflows is GA.

**Deployments:** every PR → Vercel Preview; merge to protected main → Production only after checks. Production database migration is a gated CI step, not an ad-hoc dashboard action.


## 18. Observability, Reliability and Cost

**Trace context:** `trace_id`, `request_id`, `tenant_id`, `user_id`, `mission_id`, `correlation_id` where applicable.

**Observe four layers:** technical metrics/logs/traces; security/audit; AI tokens/cost/latency/quality; commercial funnel metrics.

**Business metrics:** cost per held qualified meeting; meeting→opportunity; opportunity→proposal; proposal→contract; contract→cash; time-to-cash; repeat mission rate; buyer acceptance; node verification rate; node fraud/rejection; corridor gross contribution.

**Cost attribution:** record AI/data/human/DCG/integration cost to tenant + mission where possible. Infrastructure cost is not the main early risk; data, human research/outreach, local partners and DCG incentives can dominate.

**Target SLOs once live:** 99.9% application availability target; core mission/meeting/opportunity features must continue if an AI provider is unavailable. AI degrades gracefully rather than taking the product down.

**Backups:** Neon PITR/backups per plan, documented restore test, object-store versioning/lifecycle, recovery runbook. A backup is not accepted until restore has been tested.

2. Neon nonprod/prod provisioning; Drizzle base migration; extensions; preview-branch integration.
3. Identity/tenant/organisation model; authorization skeleton; RLS harness.
4. Audit event + domain event + outbox envelope.
5. Evidence/source/claim/verification/canonical-fact schema and file metadata.
6. Mission core + mission state machine.
7. Market/product/capability/certification/requirement taxonomies.
8. Commercial Intent + target profile.
9. Organisation relationship/private knowledge layer.
10. Target account/contact + entity-resolution workflow.
11. Outreach records + jurisdiction-policy hooks.
12. Meeting, itinerary, brief, outcome and follow-up.
13. Opportunity funnel through cash/recurring outcome.
14. Ops Console v1 and action queues.
15. Buyer magic-link flow with no-account accept/decline/request-info.
16. Client mission view + evidence request flow.
17. AI Gateway, provider registry, task registry, Gemini safe-dev adapter.
18. AI execution lineage + prompt versions + golden eval framework.
19. OpenAI and Anthropic adapters; admin route switching among configured providers.
20. DCG node profile, service area, capability and eligibility review.
21. DCG task/assignment/submission/verification.
22. Contribution attribution, reputation dimensions and append-only reward ledger.
23. Institutional cohort import/export + dashboard.
24. Vercel Workflows for durable post-meeting/evidence/report orchestration.
25. Production hardening: security headers, rate limits, malware upload scan, DSAR/retention jobs, backup restore, threat-model closure, penetration test remediation.

Every packet ships behind a feature flag where incomplete cross-module behavior could affect live users.


## 21. CI/CD Quality Gates

**Every PR:** formatting, lint, typecheck, unit tests, schema/migration validation, RLS/authorization tests, AI schema tests where relevant, dependency/security scan, Vercel Preview, Neon preview branch, Playwright smoke flow.

**Sensitive-path additional tests:**
- Cross-tenant access attempts must fail.
- Buyer magic link cannot disclose unrelated mission/private data.
- DCG ledger cannot be mutated/deleted through ordinary APIs.
- Outbox retry is idempotent.
- Duplicate webhooks do not create duplicate payouts/meetings/invoices.
- AI output cannot bypass permission/policy gate.
- Evidence verification cannot be performed by unauthorized AI/service account.

**Production promotion:** green CI, migration plan, rollback/forward-fix plan, required review, preview acceptance. High-risk schema/security changes use a canary/feature flag before broad exposure.


## 22. Cost and Speed Guardrails

**Keep early fixed infrastructure small:** Vercel + Neon + EU object storage + GitHub + monitoring; paid AI only where safe/valuable. Use synthetic public data with free Gemini during development.

**Do not buy complexity before demand:** no Kubernetes, Kafka, dedicated graph DB, Elasticsearch, warehouse, native apps, bespoke ML, autonomous outbound agents, blockchain evidence or universal tax engine initially.

**Spend where it changes commercial outcomes:** contact/company data, buyer research, human qualification, local market execution, DCG incentives, legal/compliance review and mission delivery.

**Performance principle:** normal CRUD/search pages should not wait for LLM calls. AI enrichment is async or explicitly invoked; cached/verified facts render instantly. Core mission workflows survive AI-provider failure.

**Product-speed principle:** sell/operate Mission Services from the Ops Console before building every self-service portal. The platform records all manual work in the canonical model so manual validation becomes product data rather than throwaway operations.


## 23. Production-Readiness Gates

Corridra is **not production-ready** until all mandatory gates pass:

- [ ] Full ERD and migration set reviewed.
- [ ] Mission, meeting, opportunity, evidence and DCG state machines enforced server-side.
- [ ] Permission matrix implemented + negative authorization tests.
- [ ] RLS enabled/tested on all tenant-private tables.
- [ ] Event catalogue/versioning and transactional outbox verified.
- [ ] AI task registry, provider policy and golden evaluation suite operational.
- [ ] Data classification + retention + AI-use policy mapped.
- [ ] Spain/EU outreach/legal basis reviewed by qualified counsel.
- [ ] Privacy notices, terms, DPA/SCC approach and DSAR process finalized.
- [ ] DCG terms, eligibility, contribution/reward rules and payout treatment reviewed for pilot countries.
- [ ] Threat model completed (web/API, tenancy, files, payments, GenAI/prompt injection).
- [ ] File scanning and evidence integrity controls live.
- [ ] Backup/PITR restore drill passed.
- [ ] Incident response/runbook and privileged-access process tested.
- [ ] External penetration test or equivalent independent security review completed before sensitive/high-value scale.
- [ ] Observability and alerting cover web, DB, workflows, AI and business funnel.
- [ ] Production data is isolated from previews and developer environments.
- [ ] Feature-flag rollback path exists for new high-risk features.


## 24. Deliberately Unfrozen Decisions

Do not hard-code these before field evidence:
- Final buyer/supplier match weighting.
- DCG reward/commission percentages.
- Reputation-score weights.
- Mission pricing and success economics.
- Sector/corridor expansion sequence.
- Outreach channel mix.
- Specific foundation model or embedding model.
- Automation thresholds.
- Dedicated search/warehouse/graph technology.
- Automated international payouts.

The architecture must support changing each without rewriting historical truth. Configuration is versioned, effective-dated, auditable and reversible.


## 25. Architecture Decision Records to Create First

- ADR-001 Modular monolith + domain boundaries.
- ADR-002 Neon/PostgreSQL as canonical truth.
- ADR-003 Multi-tenancy: global entities + tenant-private relationships + RLS.
- ADR-004 Evidence/claim/verification semantics.
- ADR-005 Immutable domain-event/outbox contract.
- ADR-006 Opportunity funnel and cash-based outcome semantics.
- ADR-007 DCG contribution attribution + append-only reward ledger.
- ADR-008 AI Gateway/provider abstraction + data policy.
- ADR-009 Human approval for consequential AI actions.
- ADR-010 EU-primary data + international-access/transfer controls.
- ADR-011 Vercel Workflow for durable orchestration; outbox remains source of business events.
- ADR-012 Preview database uses sanitized non-production parent only.


## 26. First Production Data Seed / Configuration

Seed only stable primitives:
- ISO countries/currencies/languages.
- Spain↔Bangladesh Corridor 01.
- Initial sectors/categories explicitly chosen for pilot.
- Mission types: outbound supplier, inbound buyer sourcing, EU→BD market entry, institutional cohort.
- Evidence verification levels and status vocabulary.
- Commercial funnel/loss reasons.
- DCG task types without fixed permanent reward values.
- Initial data classifications: PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, PERSONAL, SENSITIVE_COMMERCIAL, HIGHLY_RESTRICTED.
- Initial AI provider profiles and task policies.
- Feature flags defaulting risky/unfinished capabilities OFF.

Do not seed guessed buyer lists, supplier capabilities or "verified" claims. Seed factual taxonomies; ingest market entities with provenance.


## 27. Admin Control Plane — Minimum Complete Scope

```text
ADMIN
├─ Tenants / Users / Organisations / Memberships
├─ Roles / Permissions / Access Review
├─ Markets / Corridors / Sectors / Taxonomies
├─ Missions / Workflows / State Configuration
├─ Evidence / Verification / Entity Resolution
├─ DCG
│  ├─ Nodes / Eligibility / Tasks / Reviews
│  ├─ Contribution Attribution / Reputation
│  └─ Reward Rules / Ledger / Payout Status
├─ AI Control Center
│  ├─ Providers / Models / Credential References
│  ├─ Task Routes / Budgets / Prompts
│  ├─ Evaluations / Quality / Cost / Safety
│  └─ Human-review queues
├─ Communications / Opt-outs / Jurisdiction Policies
├─ Privacy / Consent / Retention / DSAR / Legal Hold
├─ Feature Flags / Config Versions
├─ Billing / Commercial Economics
├─ Audit / Security Events
└─ System Health / Workflows / Failed Jobs
```
Admin edits are never destructive rewrites of historical decisions. New rule versions have `effective_from`; historical records retain the rule/model/prompt version used.


## 28. Launch Scope: What Is Actually Needed to Sell

**Minimum sellable Corridra mission:**
1. Operator creates mission from a short intake.
2. Company/requirements stored as claims with provenance.
3. Ops adds/AI-suggests target accounts and records source.
4. Qualification + outreach status tracked.
5. Buyer receives frictionless secure introduction and can respond.
6. Confirmed meeting gets itinerary/brief.
7. Meeting outcome captured immediately.
8. Opportunity moves through RFQ/proposal/commitment/contract/invoice/cash.
9. Dashboard shows mission commercial yield.
10. Every step feeds the Outcome Graph.

**DCG can begin selectively:** tasks are created only where a local human materially improves information/access. Do not launch a giant community before there are paid/useful tasks.


## 29. Success Metrics for Architecture and Product

**Architecture quality:** zero cross-tenant leaks; migrations deploy safely; all consequential actions audited; restore tested; provider switch does not alter business code; AI provider outage does not break core operations.

**Operational quality:** target qualification time, meeting scheduling time, overdue follow-ups, evidence-review time, task verification time, operator actions per mission.

**Commercial quality:** held qualified meetings, qualified opportunities, RFQs, proposals, contracts, invoices, cash collected, repeat revenue, mission gross contribution.

**Network quality:** buyer acceptance, repeat buyer participation, DCG task completion/verification, contribution-to-opportunity conversion, repeat high-performing nodes.

**Moat quality:** proportion of recommendations grounded in proprietary verified outcomes/field evidence rather than generic public data; outcome-labelled relationship count; repeated corridor learning.


## 30. Final Build Rule

Corridra should become more intelligent because people use it, not more complicated because engineers build it.

**Operational action → structured event → evidence/outcome → reusable learning.**

The system must always preserve the distinction between:
- what someone claimed,
- what evidence exists,
- what was verified,
- what AI inferred,
- what humans decided,
- and what actually became commercial value/cash.

If a technical shortcut destroys that distinction, weakens tenant isolation, hides commercial truth, or locks the platform to one AI/vendor, it is not an acceptable shortcut.


## 31. Current Platform Notes / Official References

These implementation choices were checked against current official platform information at the time this canvas was generated:

- Vercel Workflows is generally available for durable, long-running execution: https://vercel.com/blog/a-new-programming-model-for-durable-execution
- Vercel Queues is currently described as public beta: https://vercel.com/changelog/vercel-queues-now-in-public-beta
- Neon/Vercel integration supports a database branch per Preview deployment: https://neon.com/blog/neon-vercel-native-integration
- Neon documents branch-first development workflows suitable for coding agents: https://neon.com/blog/branch-first-dev-loop
- Gemini API pricing/data-use terms must be checked before sending confidential/personal data; current pricing page: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing

Before production, re-check provider terms, regional availability, data processing agreements and pricing because these can change independently of Corridra's architecture.
